description: passenger_count is populated on every row
rationale: 2024-01 baseline is 4.73%; the field is not mandatory for every technology provider, so the threshold is set from the observed rate plus a margin rather than at zero. The 2025-01 rate is 15.54%, which fails this threshold - that failure is the subject of week 10.

description: payment_type is populated on every row
rationale: payment_type is needed to interpret tip and refund behaviour. Its nulls co-occur exactly with passenger_count and RatecodeID nulls: one cohort, not three independent defects.

description: dropoff_at is populated on every row
rationale: A trip with no drop-off time has no duration, so speed, duration and many consistency checks become unevaluable. One row is a defect.

description: cbd_congestion_fee is populated once the field is contractual
numerator_definition: rows in months >= applies_from where cbd_congestion_fee IS NULL
rationale: The column was added to the published yellow-taxi schema for 2025 data onwards. Before that date it did not exist, and reporting the rule as failed would be a false alarm; the rule is scoped by applies_from instead.

description: VendorID is in the documented code set
rationale: 6 appears in 2024-01 (260 rows) and 6 and 7 appear in 2025-01 (1,695 rows). A new vendor is vocabulary drift, not corrupt data - but it breaks every rule that hard-codes the vendor list, so it must surface on first appearance.

description: RatecodeID is in the documented code set
numerator_definition: rows where ratecode_id IS NOT NULL AND NOT IN (1..6)
rationale: Code 99 is undocumented and appears 28,663 times in 2024-01, almost all on one vendor. Null is counted by the completeness rules instead, not here: counting a null as an out-of-set code double-counts one defect across two dimensions.

description: payment_type is in the documented code set
numerator_definition: rows where payment_type IS NOT NULL AND NOT IN (1..6)
rationale: payment_type 0 appears on exactly the 140,162-row null cohort in 2024-01 and is not in the published code set. Zero is a sentinel, not a payment method.

numerator_definition: rows where store_and_fwd_flag IS NOT NULL AND NOT IN ('Y','N')
rationale: A two-value field that takes a third value is a transcription or contract failure, and no threshold should absorb it.

description: pickup location is a valid taxi zone
numerator_definition: rows with no matching row in the zone lookup
rationale: Referential integrity against the published lookup. Note the trap this rule cannot see: 264 and 265 are valid keys with no geography, so integrity passes where coverage fails (see cov_* rules).

description: drop-off location is a valid taxi zone
numerator_definition: rows with no matching row in the zone lookup
rationale: Same reference table as the pickup rule; kept separate because drop-off orphaning has a different cause and owner in practice.

DELIBERATELY NAIVE. 37,448 rows in 2024-01 have a negative fare, and 27,146 of them are payment_type 3 (no charge) or 4 (dispute) - documented refunds, not defects. Week 5's exercise is to measure this rule's precision on the labelled fixture (it is 0.25) and then fix or retire it.
870 rows in 2024-01 end before they start. A small rate is tolerable because the timestamp pair is vendor-supplied and clock skew is real; zero would page you for one handset.

description: total_amount equals the sum of its parts within $2.51
rationale: The naive sum-of-parts rule disagrees with 25.7% of 2024-01 rows, because one vendor's total excludes the $2.50 congestion surcharge. The tolerance absorbs that known systematic offset and leaves genuine arithmetic errors. The threshold is set just above the observed failure rate, which is itself a choice worth arguing about - that is week 5.

description: pickup falls inside the published window
numerator_definition: rows where pickup_at is before the window start or at/after the window end
rationale: 15 rows in 2024-01 predate the month and 3 follow it; the earliest pickup in the file is 2002-12-31. Kept at a tight threshold because a wrong-century timestamp usually means a broken clock or a unit error, not a late submission.

description: the constructed trip key is unique
rationale: TLC publishes no trip identifier. This key is six columns chosen by us, so zero duplicates means 'no duplicates on the key we selected', not 'no duplicate trips'. One pair of rows in 2025-01 shares all six key columns, so this rule fails that month: week 9 asks whether that pair is a vendor re-submission or a genuine collision. Any uniqueness metric is a claim about a key, and the key is part of the definition.

description: implied average speed is physically plausible
numerator_definition: rows where trip_distance > 0 and distance/duration > 80 mph
denominator_definition: rows with a positive duration and distance
rationale: PROXY ONLY. There is no ground truth for speed in this dataset. >80 mph average is implausible for a NYC taxi and stands in for 'distance or timestamp is wrong'. Do not call this an accuracy measure in the ISO/IEC 25012 sense; see week 5 on why accuracy needs a reference.

numerator_definition: rows where pu_location_id is 264 (Unknown) or 265 (Outside NYC)
rationale: Valid foreign keys that carry no geography. 31,527 trips in 2024-01 touch one of these ids, which is 1.06% - under the threshold, and still the reason a zone-level KPI would be understated.
Drop-off sentinels are more common than pickup sentinels (28,083 of the 31,527 in 2024-01), which is what you would expect from trips that leave the city.
